newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs drop 2.56 pct on U.S. rates, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs drop 2.56 pct on U.S. rates, Wall St.

text.p: Brazilian stocks fell 2.56 percent by midmorning, following Friday's sharp decline, on concerns about rising U.S. interest rates and drops in stock prices on Wall Street, brokers said.
"The market's reacting to interest rates abroad and the Dow is down," said one dealer at local Cresiful brokerage.

The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index of 47 most-traded shares, which had dropped as much as 3.14 percent, stood at 11,944 points at 1050 local/1350 GMT on volume of 102.8 million reais ($417.7 million).

Brokers said prices, still smarting from sharp drops Friday on a host of reports of a larger than expected trade gap and a Central Bank probe of several brokerages, opened lower Monday on expected declines in New York.
The Dow Jones index was off in early trade as strong economic data released in the United States sparked renewed fears of inflation and higher U.S. rates.
Locally, benchmark Telebras preferred fell as far as 3.95 percent before recouping some lost ground. The stock was down 2.63 percent at 148 reais.

Sao Paulo bourse's drop, however, was led by federal power holdiong Eletrobras's blue-chip preferred B share, which tumbled by five percent before recovering to stand at 580 reais, down 3.35 percent from the open.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index was down 1.98 percent at 3,416 points.
